23: /// How routes are stored inside a [`Router`](super::Router).
24: ///
25: /// You normally shouldn't need to care about this type. It's used in
26: /// [`Router::layer`](super::Router::layer).
27: pub struct Route<B = Body, E = Infallible>(pub(crate) BoxCloneService<Request<B>, Response, E>);
28: 
29: impl<B, E> Route<B, E> {
30:     pub(super) fn new<T>(svc: T) -> Self
31:     where
32:         T: Service<Request<B>, Response = Response, Error = E> + Clone + Send + 'static,
33:         T::Future: Send + 'static,
34:     {
35:         Self(BoxCloneService::new(svc))
36:     }
37: }
38: 
39: impl<ReqBody, E> Clone for Route<ReqBody, E> {
40:     fn clone(&self) -> Self {
41:         Self(self.0.clone())
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: impl<ReqBody, E> fmt::Debug for Route<ReqBody, E> {
46:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
47:         f.debug_struct("Route").finish()
48:     }
49: }
50: 
51: impl<B, E> Service<Request<B>> for Route<B, E> {
52:     type Response = Response;
53:     type Error = E;
54:     type Future = RouteFuture<B, E>;
55: 
56:     #[inline]
57:     fn poll_ready(&mut self, _cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
58:         Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
59:     }
60: 
61:     #[inline]
62:     fn call(&mut self, req: Request<B>) -> Self::Future {
63:         RouteFuture::new(self.0.clone().oneshot(req))
64:     }
65: }
66: 
67: pin_project! {
68:     /// Response future for [`Route`].
69:     pub struct RouteFuture<B, E> {
70:         #[pin]
71:         future: Option<Oneshot<
72:             BoxCloneService<Request<B>, Response, E>,
73:             Request<B>,
74:         >>,
75:         strip_body: bool,
76:         allow_header: Option<Bytes>,
77:     }
78: }
79: 
80: impl<B, E> RouteFuture<B, E> {
81:     pub(crate) fn new(
82:         future: Oneshot<BoxCloneService<Request<B>, Response, E>, Request<B>>,
83:     ) -> Self {
84:         RouteFuture {
85:             future: Some(future),
86:             strip_body: false,
87:             allow_header: None,
88:         }
89:     }
90: 
91:     pub(crate) fn empty() -> Self {
92:         RouteFuture {
93:             future: None,
94:             strip_body: false,
95:             allow_header: None,
96:         }
97:     }

100:         self.strip_body = strip_body;
101:         self
102:     }
103: 
104:     pub(crate) fn allow_header(mut self, allow_header: Bytes) -> Self {
105:         self.allow_header = Some(allow_header);
106:         self
107:     }
108: 
109:     pub(crate) fn call_method_router(
110:         mut self,
111:         methods: &MethodRouter<B, E>,
112:         fallback: &Route<B, E>,
113:         req: Request<B>,
114:     ) -> Self {
115:         let mut parts = RequestParts::new(req);
116:         let method = parts.method().clone();
117:         let req = parts
118:             .try_into_request()
119:             .expect("request body was missing");
120: 
121:         self.strip_body = method == http::Method::HEAD;
122: 
123:         macro_rules! call {
124:             (
125:                 $req:expr,
126:                 $method:expr,
127:                 $method_variant:ident,
128:                 $svc:expr
129:             ) => {
130:                 if $method == http::Method::$method_variant {
131:                     if let Some(svc) = $svc {
132:                         self.future = Some(svc.0.clone().oneshot($req));
133:                         return self;
134:                     }
135:                 }
136:             };
137:         }
138: 
139:         call!(req, method, HEAD, &methods.head);
140:         call!(req, method, HEAD, &methods.get);
141:         call!(req, method, GET, &methods.get);
142:         call!(req, method, POST, &methods.post);
143:         call!(req, method, OPTIONS, &methods.options);
144:         call!(req, method, PATCH, &methods.patch);
145:         call!(req, method, PUT, &methods.put);
146:         call!(req, method, DELETE, &methods.delete);
147:         call!(req, method, TRACE, &methods.trace);
148: 
149:         self.future = Some(fallback.0.clone().oneshot(req));
150:         self
151:     }
152: }

159:         let strip_body = self.strip_body;
160:         let allow_header = self.allow_header.take();
161: 
162:         let future = self
163:             .project()
164:             .future
165:             .as_pin_mut()
166:             .expect("RouteFuture polled before a service was bound");
167: 
168:         match future.poll(cx) {
169:             Poll::Ready(Ok(res)) => {
170:                 let mut res = if strip_body {
171:                     res.map(|_| boxed(Empty::new()))
172:                 } else {
173:                     res
174:                 };
175: 
176:                 match allow_header {

179:                             header::ALLOW,
180:                             HeaderValue::from_maybe_shared(allow_header)
181:                                 .expect("invalid `Allow` header"),
182:                         );
183:                     }
184:                     _ => {}
185:                 }
186: 
187:                 Poll::Ready(Ok(res))
188:             }
189:             Poll::Ready(Err(err)) => Poll::Ready(Err(err)),
190:             Poll::Pending => Poll::Pending,
191:         }
192:     }
193: }

5: mod for_handlers {

7:     use http::HeaderMap;

9:     #[tokio::test]
10:     async fn get_handles_head() {
11:         let app = Router::new().route(
12:             "/",
13:             get(|| async {
14:                 let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
15:                 headers.insert("x-some-header", "foobar".parse().unwrap());
16:                 (headers, "you shouldn't see this")
17:             }),
18:         );
19: 
20:         // don't use reqwest because it always strips bodies from HEAD responses
21:         let res = app
22:             .oneshot(
23:                 Request::builder()
24:                     .uri("/")
25:                     .method(Method::HEAD)
26:                     .body(Body::empty())
27:                     .unwrap(),
28:             )
29:             .await
30:             .unwrap();
31: 
32:         assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
33:         assert_eq!(res.headers()["x-some-header"], "foobar");
34: 
35:         let body = hyper::body::to_bytes(res.into_body()).await.unwrap();
36:         assert_eq!(body.len(), 0);
37:     }
38: }

part.text:
Fix complete. Changes in `axum/src/routing/route.rs`:

- In `RouteFuture::poll` (axum/src/routing/route.rs:171), when handling `HEAD` requests, the response's original body size hint is now read *before* the body is replaced with an empty one. If the size is exact, a `content-length` header with that value is inserted (axum/src/routing/route.rs:181), so a `HEAD` reply reports the same length as the corresponding `GET` reply instead of `0`.

Verified: all 144 `axum` lib tests pass, including the previously failing `head_content_length_through_hyper_server` and `head_content_length_through_hyper_server_that_hits_fallback` (which also covers the fallback path via `call_method_router`).
